correctness.rationale: The 14 right/left rotation orbits are vertex-disjoint directed cycles, including the two loops. Any minimum set must delete at least one vertex per orbit. Independently tested the given 14-vertex witness, so the minimum cardinality is exactly 14. I enumerated all 181,398,528 labeled one-per-orbit transversals with no partial-graph pruning. In each full survivor set A I iterated A <- A intersect N+(A), with N+ the outgoing-neighbor union. A vertex surviving t rounds is the endpoint of a residual walk of t edges; a nonempty fixed point means a directed cycle, and on a DAG the round giving the empty set is the longest path in vertices. The exact count and all 14 histogram bins agreed. Complement is a digraph automorphism and reversal an orientation-reversing isomorphism; both preserve the vertex length. On the 408 minimizers, exhaustive independent action evaluation gives fixed counts 408,0,0,4 for identity/complement/reversal/reverse-complement. Burnside gives 103 orbits, two of size two (both canonical masks match) and 101 of size four. The 48-at-26 endpoint and optimizer percentage also agree.
residual_risks: Exact for the labeled binary order-six digraph and the vertex-count convention only.

value.rationale: The graph and optimization measure are motivated by the earlier study of exact residual-path guarantees over all minimum decycling sets. The known total and extrema hide how rare either endpoint is. The exact frequency and stabilizer census resolve that gap at a size with tens of thousands of admissible sets, giving reference data for exact graph algorithms and optimizer enumeration; the symmetry result also states which involution accounts for the exceptional smaller orbits. This is not a recomputation offered as new of the known endpoints.
residual_risks: No performance conclusion for other graph orders or contexts.
